team_fix.why: In 2021 the Blue Jays played at Dunedin through May, then Buffalo from June 1, then returned to Toronto July 30, so the homes were out of time order.
The Indians played the entire 1933 season at Cleveland Municipal Stadium before returning to League Park for 1934.
The 1939 Indianapolis ABCs were the relocated Atlanta Black Crackers, not the 1938 ABCs club (which became the St. Louis Stars).

washington-park-ii.why: Washington Park II opened April 30, 1898; 1883 is the opening of the first Washington Park.

forbes-field.why: Listed point is downtown Pittsburgh, about 3 km from the known Forbes Field site in Oakland on Roberto Clemente Drive.

greenlee-field.why: Listed point is the city center; the site is on Bedford Avenue in the Hill District, marked by a historical marker.

missing: All 1920-1932 Negro league seasons (NNL1, ECL, ANL, EWL, NSL) are absent from the listing, although data/history/raw/negro_1920_1932.json holds 64 team stints and 47 parks; it appears to have been dropped in the merge.
Chicago American Giants, NNL1 1920-1931, and as Cole's American Giants in the NSL 1932.
Detroit Stars, NNL1 1920-1931; St. Louis Stars, NNL1 1922-1931; St. Louis Giants, NNL1 1920-1921; Chicago Giants, NNL1 1920-1921; Dayton Marcos, NNL1 1920 and 1926.
Cuban Stars (West), NNL1 1920-1930; Indianapolis ABCs, NNL1 1920-1926 (out mid-1924) and a second ABCs club in 1931.

Birmingham Black Barons and Memphis Red Sox, NNL1 1924-1925 and 1927-1930; Nashville Elite Giants, NNL1 1930; Columbus Buckeyes 1921; Cleveland Tate Stars 1922-1923; Toledo Tigers 1923; Pittsburgh Keystones 1922; Milwaukee Bears 1923; Cleveland Browns 1924; Cleveland Elites 1926; Cleveland Hornets 1927; Cleveland Tigers 1928; Cleveland Cubs and Louisville White Sox 1931 (all NNL1).

ECL clubs: Bacharach Giants, Baltimore Black Sox, Brooklyn Royal Giants, Cuban Stars (East), Lincoln Giants 1923-1928; Hilldale 1923-1927; Harrisburg Giants 1924-1927; Washington/Wilmington Potomacs 1924-1925; Newark Stars 1926; Philadelphia Tigers 1928 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Colored_League).
ANL 1929: Bacharach Giants, Baltimore Black Sox, Cuban Stars (East), Hilldale, Lincoln Giants, Homestead Grays (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Negro_League).
EWL 1932: Detroit Wolves, Homestead Grays, Baltimore Black Sox, Cuban Stars, Hilldale, Washington Pilots, Cleveland Stars, Newark Browns (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East%E2%80%93West_League).

NSL 1932: Atlanta Black Crackers, Cole's American Giants, Columbus Turf Club, Indianapolis ABCs, Louisville Black Caps, Memphis Red Sox, Monroe Monarchs, Montgomery Grey Sox, Nashville Elite Giants (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Negro_Southern_League_(1920%E2%80%931936)).
Homestead Grays, NNL2 1933: Wikipedia lists the Grays in the Negro National League in 1933 (1934 disputed), but the listing starts them in 1935 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homestead_Grays).

Akron's 1933 home park is known: the Columbus Blue Birds/Akron Grays/Cleveland Giants club played at League Park II in Akron, so akron-unknown-grounds should be replaced by a real park record (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akron_Grays).
